steps.what: Choose poster message, programme facts and display concept
Lay out posters and display panels in standard formats
Review the poster design and release the final version

tasks.design: Configure repeatable layouts in {OTHER}, the existing design editor, from a technician-authored brief. Keep message selection, proof review and release human; this only removes repeated layout operations.
tasks.previous_blocker: Recurring formats are laid out afresh.
tasks.enabler_now: Template fields and overflow checks can produce consistent proofs.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing an appealing message and judging legibility in the intended space.
tasks.human_edge: The technician understands the community and display context.
tasks.altitude: Spend less time resizing recurring designs, with unchanged creative responsibility.

evidence.claim: Template-based layout can remove repetitive formatting while leaving message design and proof judgement human; estimated saving is E1.

assumptions: Boundary is design and release, excluding physical installation and programme planning.

Technician produces title, body copy, date, time, location, booking instructions, image selection and target dimensions in s1. Its full 40 hours include writing, rights checks and field entry; missing facts are confirmed manually there.
Template renderer produces a draft only and flags overflow for s3; unusual designs fall back to manual layout in the retained review allowance or reduce savings.
Test native editor templates first. Five focal upkeep hours maintain layouts and test prints per 100 baseline hours.
research_questions: How much layout time remains after field capture, overflow fixes and proof review?

approvals.approved_version: Exact rendered poster proof including wording, dates, images and dimensions; any change voids release approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=40+0+20=60; gross 40 minus 5 upkeep gives net 35. Low 10 allows 25 hours of bespoke layout fixes. Creative selection and final review retain time; E1.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Verify borrower identification and capture card issue details
Populate and produce the borrower identification card
Check and issue the identification card to the borrower

tasks.design: Configure card generation in the {OTHER} library system from the verified borrower record. The technician still verifies identity, handles the card and checks it before issue.
tasks.previous_blocker: Borrower details are sometimes retyped into a separate card tool.
tasks.enabler_now: Native card templates can reuse verified fields.
tasks.still_hard: Identity discrepancies, replacements and unreadable cards.
tasks.human_edge: The technician resolves identity and access exceptions.
tasks.altitude: Less duplicate card entry with unchanged issue responsibility.

evidence.claim: Library card templates can reuse verified borrower fields, saving only manual re-entry where it exists.

assumptions: Boundary is issue of a card, excluding initial membership registration already completed elsewhere.
Technician produces borrower identifier, display name, card type, expiry, replacement status and identity-check outcome in s1; its 40 hours include verification and entering missing values manually.
Machine s2 removes only re-entry and layout. Printer handling and physical card checks remain in s3; existing printing runtime earns no labour saving.
Use native card settings first. Four focal upkeep hours cover template and card-reader tests per 100 baseline hours.
research_questions: Does native card generation remove entry effort without increasing identity exceptions?

approvals.approved_version: Exact physical card identifier, displayed borrower details and linked account checked before handover; changes require recheck

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=40+0+25=65; gross 35 less 4 upkeep gives net 31 for duplicate-entry sites. Low 0 represents already integrated card issue, where deployment is declined. E1; no physical handling saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Review subject matter and capture identifying material
Find candidate classification numbers and subject headings

loop.purpose: Suggest subject headings from the material's content
loop.input: Captured subject evidence and approved vocabulary
loop.output: Ranked headings with supporting passages and uncertainty
loop.check: Technician checks that headings represent the main subject rather than incidental terms; code checks valid vocabulary identifiers
loop.stop: One revised suggestion then manual classification for ambiguity or absent coverage
loop.why_not_simpler: Valid codes do not establish the material's actual subject; semantic interpretation is needed

steps.what: Select and record classification numbers and headings

tasks.design: Use validated heading suggestions in the {OTHER} catalogue after checking native authority lookup. The technician selects the final classification based on the actual material and local policy.
tasks.previous_blocker: Subject terminology does not map cleanly to controlled headings.
tasks.enabler_now: Assisted keyword assignment exists, while final classification remains contextual.
tasks.still_hard: Interdisciplinary materials and locally preferred classifications.
tasks.human_edge: The technician recognises the principal subject and local collection context.
tasks.altitude: Less candidate lookup, with classification decisions unchanged.

reach.learn: Vocabulary scope notes and local policy

evidence.claim: Annif supports assisted subject suggestions and was tested by the KB on the Dutch Brinkman thesaurus; this does not validate autonomous classification numbers.

assumptions: Boundary is subject classification only. If performed during descriptive cataloguing, assign this effort to one task rather than summing both estimates.
Technician produces item identifier, title, abstract or contents excerpt and subject observations within s1's full 30 hours. Missing text is transcribed or read manually there.

Librarian maintains existing vocabulary identifiers, preferred labels and scope notes. Additional vocabulary review costs two other-role hours; focal monitoring costs four hours per 100 baseline hours.
Use native authority and shared-record lookup before introducing suggestions. No model-generated classification is written without s3.
research_questions: Do accepted heading suggestions reduce lookup time after capture and semantic checks?

approvals.approved_version: Exact item identifier, classification numbers, heading identifiers and vocabulary version; edits void acceptance

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=30+24+30=84; gross 16 minus 4 upkeep gives net 12. Low 4 allows eight extra hours for difficult subject matches; E1 scenarios.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Verify the interlibrary loan request and capture lending conditions
Submit the loan request and record partner acknowledgements
Handle received materials, exceptions and patron collection

tasks.design: Configure native interlibrary request exchange between {OTHER} and {PARTNER_PORTAL}, keeping the technician's final submission check. Status reuse removes retyping; physical handling and partner exceptions retain their time.
tasks.previous_blocker: Loan details and acknowledgements are copied between systems.
tasks.enabler_now: Native exchange can reuse validated request fields and partner status.
tasks.still_hard: Edition substitutions, fees, restrictions and missing materials.
tasks.human_edge: The technician checks whether a proposed loan meets the patron's need.
tasks.altitude: Less request re-entry with unchanged external commitment authority.

evidence.claim: Native interlibrary exchange can reduce duplicate request and status entry where supported; this workflow and saving are E1 assumptions.

assumptions: Boundary covers the local technician's loan processing, excluding partner library search and shipping labour, which remain unchanged.

Technician produces patron identifier, item identifier, requested edition, lender identifier, fee limit, delivery destination and needed-by date in s1. Its full 40 hours include capture and checking restrictions; missing fields are resolved manually.

Partner librarian produces acknowledgement identifier, status, due date and restrictions in existing lending work. No new partner capture is required; unstructured acknowledgements are handled manually inside s2's remaining 17.5 hours.
Test native exchange before custom integration. Four focal hours cover exception monitoring; two other-role support hours maintain access per 100 focal baseline hours.
research_questions: Does native exchange reduce submission work after final checks and unsupported partner messages?

already_counted.description: Check exact submission and handle unsupported acknowledgements

approvals.approved_version: Exact lender, item and edition, patron, destination, fee limit and requested dates; edits void submission approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=40+17.5+25=82.5; gross 17.5 minus 4 upkeep gives net 13.5. Low 4 allows 9.5 additional manual exchange hours. Partner and physical labour earn no reduction; E1.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Reduce repeated layout and data entry while keeping classification judgement and physical library service.
reach: Support librarian review of subject and lending exceptions
role.ambitious_version: A technician who spends less time copying details and more time resolving useful service questions.
